text.text_excerpt: So if you find your sweet tooth waking you in the middle of the night, you should head uptown to Insomnia Cookies! I had the macadamia nut, the m&m cookie and the chocolate chunk and all were handed to me nice and warm and soft and gooey and delicious! A cold glass of milk is the perfect compliment to this sweet treat, which they sell along with a few ice creams that you can have made into an ice cream//cookie sandwich! I only gave them 4 stars because even though they are on a rather busy section of Maple street, they, unlike some of the other businesses, have no parking. AND, there's a troll that lives next door and likes to harass you for parking in front of Insomina Cookie! Other than...

Such a fangirl when it comes to Insomnia Cookies. For years in college, I watched in agony as my internet friends indulged in warm, gooey cookies from this place. I saw them getting cookies delivered in the late night hour and sharing such bliss by Instagramming each morsel to torture me. And then, Insomnia came to New Orleans. Surprisingly enough, Insomnia arrived on Maple immediately after I graduated from college. What a bust, I thought. Until I moved uptown and visited this spot after one too many whiskey cokes at Bruno's. (my collegiate stomping grounds, might I add. While I'm at it, Tulanians, you should beat it. Bruno's is Loyolo territory, fam. And don't you forget it.) Anywho, I ...

I first found out about this place in an Eater New Orleans article last year so I was pretty excited to finally try this place out almost a year later. A lot of students get caught up with studying and sometimes have to pull all nighters. You either have a bunch of snacks lined up to tackle the night or you simple have no snacks and are craving something sweet. If it's the latter, then Insomnia Cookies has just what you need because they close at 3AM every night! The moment I found out this place opened, I stopped by to grab a few cookies for my friends and me. Before stopping by, I tried to order online for takeout but the ready times were unbelievably long. I assume it was made-to-order...
